newsitem.title: USA: Mo. House to take up expanded investment measure.
newsitem.headline: Mo. House to take up expanded investment measure.

text.p: - The Missouri House could give final approval this week to a proposed constitutional amendment expanding the investment powers of the state treasurer.

Gene Rose, communications director for the House, said that lawmakers gave preliminary approval to the measure on Tuesday and could take it up for a final vote later this week. If approved, the measure would move on to the Senate, he said.

The resolution would place a proposed constitutional amendment on the 1998 ballot requiring the state treasurer to prepare an investment policy that would include an asset allocation plan allowing a limited amount of state funds to be invested in domestically issued bankers acceptances and corporate commercial paper.
The amendment, which has the support of State Treasurer Bob Holden, would also extend the maximum investment period for state funds not needed for current expenses to five years from three years.
